findings.text: The fragment says 'The head arm passes four tests in 8.13 s (after-suite.log, EXIT=0)', but after-suite.log - the log it cites - reports '4 passed in 16.94s'. The cited log does not carry the stated wall time, so a reader checking the claim against its own source finds a number that does not reconcile. The substance (four passing tests, EXIT=0, no added failures) is correct and independently reproduced; the wall time is a record-accuracy defect.

The fragment cites render-only.log as the record of the panel regeneration, but that log's header reads 'revision: 18c30b9a' (the base) while the SVGs it produced carry the repaired titles (110/300). The render ran with the fix uncommitted in the worktree, so the log's stamped revision names the code that would still have drawn -110. A reader reconciling the log's revision against its output reaches a contradiction the record does not explain; a one-line note that the render preceded the commit, or a re-stamped log, would remove it.

test_no_drawn_title_prints_a_negative_cell_count reads only the SVG text comments and fails only when a comment contains a negative integer; it does not assert that any title comment was read, nor that the expected magnitude (110/300) is present. An SVG that carried no text comments at all - or a panel that dropped its cell-count title - yields offenders == {} and the test passes, so the guard's protection is vacuous exactly when it is most needed. Asserting the presence of the expected cell-count titles (or that the comment list is non-empty and carries the receipt's magnitudes) would make the red/green boundary unconditional.

gate_arms_note: added_failure_count/added_failure_ids are derived from the reviewed run's own arms: baseline_suite revision 18c30b9a, command 'JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261003T161635421340-fsa-gate-b-cell-count-magnitude-render/base-arm/tests/test_frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py', completed true, exit_status 0, failure_count 0, failure_ids []; after_suite revision b1bfc43c, command 'JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py', completed true, exit_status 0, failure_count 0, failure_ids []. Both arms ran to their pytest summary line (3 passed / 4 passed), so added_failure_count = 0 and added_failure_ids = []. The after arm collects four tests against the base arm's three: the one added test is the new title guard, not a failure. Independently reproduced by this review at the reviewed head in a scratch extraction (review-gate.log: 4 passed, EXIT=0) and the declared control against the pre-repair panels (review-negative-control.log: 1 failed, EXIT=1).

justifications.durability: The rule is pinned by a real, falsifiable test that demonstrably fires: test_no_drawn_title_prints_a_negative_cell_count reddens on the pre-repair panels under the declared control, which I reproduced first-hand (1 failed, EXIT=1), so it is not merely a passing guard. It sits in the existing gate file that the plan's painter rulings already exercise. Weaknesses that keep it below full marks. The test scans only the SVG text comments (re.findall(r'<!-- (.*?) -->')); it asserts that no comment carries a negative integer, but does not assert that any drawn title was read. An SVG whose text comments were absent - a matplotlib change, or a panel that draws no titles - yields offenders={} and the test passes vacuously, so the guard can go blind rather than red. Nor does it assert that the expected magnitude (110/300) is present: a title that dropped the cell count entirely would also pass. The companion test test_render_only_reproduces_receipted_panel_set pins the comment lists to the regenerated panels, which mitigates but does not close this, since it compares two artifacts that could both lose their comments. The check is also the only thing wiring the repair to a test; nothing else imports the driver.
justifications.evidence: The gate is recorded and independently reproduced. The reviewed run's baseline-suite.log shows 3 passed EXIT=0 at 18c30b9a in a scratch base-arm extraction, and after-suite.log shows 4 passed EXIT=0 at b1bfc43c in the worktree. I re-ran the same four tests at the reviewed head in a scratch extraction under $TMPDIR (review-gate.log, module.__file__ = <scratch>/benchmarks/frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py, cwd = <scratch>): 4 passed, EXIT=0. I reproduced the declared negative control first-hand: extracting the pre-repair panels with 'git show 18c30b9a:docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/gate-b/<name>' and running the new assertion against them via NOVA_FROZEN_CURRENT_PANEL_DIR gives 1 failed, EXIT=1 (review-negative-control.log), the same signature the run's negative-control.log carries (the assertion lists all six signed error titles and the signed suptitle). Deductions. (a) The evidence fragment states the head arm 'passes four tests in 8.13 s' and cites after-suite.log, but that log's summary line reads '4 passed in 16.94s' - the cited log does not carry the stated wall time (finding 1). (b) render-only.log is stamped 'revision: 18c30b9a' (the base), yet its recorded output is the repaired figures (titles 110/300); it was produced while the fix was uncommitted, so its revision header names code that would have drawn -110, and a reader reconciling the two is misled (finding 2). The after-suite arm is authoritative and unaffected.
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic: a four-line source change plus one focused test, no new dependency, no new abstraction, no plan/sprint/ticket identifier in names, comments or subject lines. It follows the file's own existing override idiom by adding NOVA_FROZEN_CURRENT_PANEL_DIR alongside the pre-existing NOVA_FROZEN_CURRENT_RECEIPT so the declared control can point the assertion at the base panels. It matches the moment-order repair of the same finding already on main (titles composed from abs(requested_cells)). The regenerated panels follow the plotting rules already governing this figure family; no caption was rewritten to describe the defect away. No fit deduction beyond the guard's narrowness, scored under durability.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal - repair the gate-b cell-count sign so both title sites print the count as a magnitude, without disturbing the analytic content of the panels - is met and independently reproduced. The diff is exactly four source lines: benchmarks/frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py:1159 (error-panel title) and :1220 (comparison suptitle) now compose abs(row['requested_cells']); the signed requested_cells field is unchanged in receipt.json and parts/*.json. I read the title comments back out of both committed SVGs: absolute-flux-error.svg prints weak-rotation-reactor-static 110 / moderate-rotation-conventional-static 110 / strong-rotation-compact-static 110 / diverted-single-null 110 / weak-rotation-reactor-static 300 / diverted-single-null 300, i.e. six titles now 110/110/110/110/300/300, and weak-110-frozen-prediction-analytic-terminal.svg's suptitle prints ...110. At the base revision the identical readback gives -110/-300 (git show 18c30b9a:...: six signed error titles plus the signed suptitle), so the defect is real and the repair closes it. The error magnitudes in every title (max |error| ... Wb = ... span) are byte-identical to base apart from the cell-count token, so only what is drawn changed. Not full marks only because the record's own prose misstates the head arm's wall time (finding on the fragment, evidence dimension).
justifications.scope_discipline: The reviewed range 18c30b9a..b1bfc43c touches exactly five paths - benchmarks/frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py, tests/test_frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py, docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/gate-b/absolute-flux-error.svg, docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/gate-b/weak-110-frozen-prediction-analytic-terminal.svg, and docs/evidence/fragments/figure-and-solver-audit/fsa-gate-b-cell-count-magnitude-render.html - all inside the run's granted write paths. No plan, shared index, solver source or concurrent-node path is touched (no nova/ file appears in the diff). The commit carries a conventional subject and a two-paragraph body explaining what changed and why; a trailer scan over the body returns no AI attribution and a label scan over the two source files returns no plan/sprint/ticket identifier. The single commit is the whole change.
